title: Social Perception of Faces in a Vision-Language Model

bias_targets.methodology: Computing the difference in cosine similarity between CLIP embeddings of race-varied face images (synthetic and real) and text prompts representing validated social psychology traits (e.g., Warmth, Competence). The paper also evaluates racial associations using Adapted SC-WEAT, Markedness, and Skew@k metrics.

Computing the difference in cosine similarity between CLIP embeddings of gender-varied face images (synthetic and real) and text prompts representing validated social psychology traits. Gender associations are also evaluated using Adapted SC-WEAT, Markedness, and Skew@k metrics.
Computing the difference in cosine similarity between CLIP embeddings of face images incrementally manipulated or annotated by age and text prompts representing validated social psychology traits.

Analyzing the combined intersectional effects of race, gender, and age (e.g., examining the unique trait perception trajectories of Black women) on the cosine similarity between face image embeddings and social trait text embeddings.
